question: With physics paced to the wall clock, how many physical ticks does policy latency consume, and how many of the 8 planned action slots become unexecutable (STALE) as a declared worker return delay grows?
pacing: tick k starts no earlier than anchor + k*pace_factor*dt (16.667 ms); late ticks do not sleep and lag is recorded; the sense phase (render, packet, start) happens only with no ticket in flight, before dispatch, and its duration shifts the anchor (not physical time)

predictions.identity_check_not_finding: for every returned ticket with an empty queue at return, STALE slots == min(8, return_tick - start_tick), since desired ticks are start+1..start+8 and the earliest legal tick is return_tick + 1
predictions.basis: elapsed ~ ceil((compute ~5 ms + IPC + declared delay) / 16.667 ms) + at most one tick of owner polling granularity

guard.on_violation: STOP: no further apply/start; pending commands DROPPED; in-flight ticket awaited without physics, else censored

target_admission: finite 9D target inside actual native joint limits, else CHANNEL_RESULT REJECTED and the previous target is held; no clipping

policy.model: prior P0 engineering checkpoint (same bytes as NA1); actions known to be inaccurate
policy.worker: separate CPU process, CUDA hidden, fixed noise seed, 16-step deterministic DDIM, then declared return delay (sleep)
policy.chunk: desired ticks request_tick+1..+8; slots earlier than current_tick+latency at return are STALE, never re-timed

claims_allowed: physics advanced at the paced rate while the worker computed (per-ticket elapsed ticks from the journal; lag distribution from the tick log)
number of planned slots made STALE by latency, per declared delay
returned slots applied only at original ticks, at most one per tick, FIFO; byte-reserved journal closed
native camera frames at every request tick
claims_excluded: policy quality or VLA time accuracy
a strong-timer baseline (E02 requires it; not run here)
